name: Animated Map Route
summary: A stylised map with a dotted route drawing between four cities while a small vehicle follows it.
bestFor: Travel, logistics and delivery route explainers
prompt: Create an animated route map for a made-up four-stop journey across an abstract map with hand-drawn landmasses. Pop each city label as the route reaches it, draw a dotted line between the stops, and send a small vehicle along the path. Pause briefly at each stop to name it, then finish by showing the whole route lit up with a one-line summary of the trip.

name: API Request Flow Explainer
summary: A request packet crosses client, gateway, service and database; the response returns and the status turns green.
bestFor: Explaining how an API call travels through a backend
prompt: Explain what happens when an app calls an API. Follow one request from the client through the gateway and the service to the database, then follow the response back. Show what each hop does, where authentication happens, and how the status code tells the client the call succeeded.

name: Pastel Dawn Landscape
summary: A low-poly hill landscape under a pastel dawn sky, with drifting clouds and a slow camera glide.
bestFor: Travel, wellness, mindful app and nature brand intros
prompt: Make a calm opening for a mindfulness app called Dawn. Glide slowly over soft low-poly hills under a pastel sunrise with drifting clouds and a gentle glow in the sky. Introduce the app with a short line, show what it helps with in a few quiet beats, and finish on an invitation to begin the morning.

name: Animated Bar Chart Race
summary: Six example bars overtake each other as a year counter ticks, with the current leader highlighted.
bestFor: Showing how rankings change over time
prompt: Make a bar chart race about how six made-up groups, labelled A to F, rank over six years. Start with all bars short and sorted, then let a year counter tick forward while the bars grow and slide past each other. Highlight whichever bar leads at each moment, call out the biggest overtake, and finish on the final ranking with a one-line takeaway.

name: Bayes Theorem Boxes
summary: A unit square is split into areas that resize when evidence arrives, turning a prior into a posterior.
bestFor: Probability explainers, statistics lessons
prompt: Explain Bayes theorem with areas. Split a unit square into the hypothesis and its opposite, mark the share of each side where the evidence appears, then throw away everything without evidence and stretch what remains back to a full square. The new proportion is the updated belief, shown beside the prior.

name: Binary Search Explainer
summary: A precise math-channel explainer: a highlighted range halves three times until the target number is found.
bestFor: Teaching algorithms and why halving is fast
prompt: Explain binary search with sixteen sorted number boxes. Ask for one target value, point at the middle box, and say whether the target is higher or lower. Dim the half that cannot contain it and let the highlighted range shrink. Repeat until one box is left and it lights up green. Close by contrasting the few steps taken with checking every box in turn.

name: Chalkboard Formula Lesson
summary: Chalk writes a right-triangle formula and draws its figure on a dusty board, then a hand wipes a line clean.
bestFor: Math and physics lessons in a classic classroom style
prompt: Teach the Pythagorean theorem on a chalkboard. Write the heading, then the formula for the sides of a right triangle. Draw a right triangle with the right angle marked and label the two short sides and the long side. Write a worked example with the numbers three, four and five, then wipe that line away with an eraser while the narrator summarises the rule.

name: Blockchain Explainer
summary: Blocks link by hash; tamper with one and every later link breaks red.
bestFor: Teaching how hash-linked chains stay tamper-evident
prompt: Explain how a blockchain keeps its records honest. Show blocks that each carry the hash of the block before them, forming a chain. Then change the data in one earlier block and watch its hash change, so every later link no longer matches. End on why that makes tampering easy to spot.

name: Cache and Database Explainer
summary: A request misses the cache, hits the database, fills the cache, then the next request is served instantly.
bestFor: Explaining caching to engineers and new hires
prompt: Explain how a cache sits in front of a database. Follow one request: it checks the cache first and misses, so it asks the database. The answer comes back and is stored in the cache. Then show the next identical request being served straight from the cache. Close on why this keeps the database calm.

name: CI/CD Pipeline Explainer
summary: A commit moves through build, test and deploy stages, each earning a checkmark before the live badge.
bestFor: Explaining automated build, test and release flows
prompt: Explain how a CI/CD pipeline takes a code change to production. Follow one commit through the build stage, the automated tests and the deployment, showing what each stage checks and what happens when a stage fails. Finish on the change running live for users and why small, frequent releases are safer.

name: Code Diff Walkthrough
summary: A two-pane code diff: old lines fade out in red, new lines slide in green, a chip names the change.
bestFor: Refactor explainers, code-review recaps and changelog videos
prompt: Make a short video explaining one refactor as a code diff. Show the old version on the left and the new version on the right in a dark theme with syntax colours. The removed lines fade out in red, the replacement lines slide in green, and a caption chip names the change while a voiceover explains why it is simpler.

name: Coding Agent Loop Explainer
summary: An agent loop lights up in turn: read goal, plan, use tools, check, report.
bestFor: Explaining how AI coding agents work in a loop
prompt: Explain how a coding agent works. Walk around the loop one step at a time: it reads the goal, makes a plan, uses tools such as reading files and running tests, checks its own work, and reports back. Make clear that the loop repeats until the goal is met and the checks pass.

name: Data Centre Fly-Through
summary: A camera glides down a glowing server-rack corridor into fog, LEDs blinking and cables pulsing.
bestFor: Cloud, hosting and infrastructure launches
prompt: A cinematic fly-through of a dark data centre. The camera glides down a long corridor of server racks, their tiny lights blinking in cyan and amber, glowing cables running along the floor into the fog. Close on a short line about reliable infrastructure that never sleeps.

name: Derivative as Slope
summary: A dark-navy graph where a curve is drawn and a point slides along it, its tangent and slope readout updating.
bestFor: Calculus intros, tutoring channels, course teasers
prompt: Explain what a derivative is. Draw a smooth curve on a graph, slide a point along it with its tangent line, and show the slope number changing from negative to positive. Then trace the slope itself as a second curve, so the idea that the derivative is the rate of change becomes visible.

name: Donut Chart With Counters
summary: A donut chart draws its coloured segments clockwise while three example counters count up beside it.
bestFor: Share-of-total breakdowns with headline numbers
prompt: Make a data summary with a donut chart on the left and three big counters on the right, using clearly made-up numbers. Draw the four donut segments clockwise in different colours, one after another, with a short label for each. While the chart fills in, count the three numbers up from zero and slide each one in with its name. End on the complete donut and all three final numbers.

name: Eigenvectors Visual Explainer
summary: A 3Blue1Brown-style grid transform where most arrows turn but two special ones only stretch along their line.
bestFor: Linear algebra lessons and data science intros
prompt: Explain eigenvectors visually. Show a flat coordinate grid with a handful of arrows, then apply a linear transformation and watch the grid shear and stretch. Point out that most arrows are knocked off their original line, while two special arrows stay on theirs and only change length. Name the stretch factors, write the equation A v equals lambda v, and say why these directions are useful for understanding the matrix.

name: Exponential Growth Explainer
summary: A calm math-channel graph: a curve doubles at equal time steps while the y axis keeps rescaling to hold it.
bestFor: Explaining compounding, growth and scale intuition
prompt: Explain exponential growth with a single curve. Draw the axes, then let the quantity double at every equal tick of time and mark each doubling with a dot. Show how the vertical axis has to rescale again and again just to keep the curve in view. Contrast it with steady addition, and finish on the idea that a constant doubling time means the curve eventually outruns any straight line.

name: Flat vector biology explainer
summary: A friendly round cell pinches in the middle and divides into two, its organelles drifting into each half.
bestFor: Biology lessons and school science explainers
prompt: Make a flat vector biology explainer about how a cell divides. Start with one friendly round cell with a nucleus and a few small organelles. Show the nucleus splitting, the cell stretching and pinching in the middle, and two new cells drifting apart. Explain each step in simple words, with bold colours on a deep purple background.

name: Flat vector clean energy explainer
summary: A sun, a wind turbine and a battery send glowing power lines into a flat-colour city whose windows light up.
bestFor: Energy, sustainability and utility explainers
prompt: Make a flat vector explainer about how clean energy reaches a city. Show a sun, a spinning wind turbine and a battery as the sources, then draw glowing power lines that join at a hub and run into a small city of colourful buildings. Light the windows one by one as the power arrives, and explain each step in plain, friendly words.

name: Flat vector space explainer
summary: Friendly flat-colour planets orbit a glowing sun, with moons, parallax stars and a labelled planet.
bestFor: Astronomy lessons and kids' science explainers
prompt: Make a friendly flat vector explainer about the solar system. Show the sun with a gentle glow, then let each planet pop in on its own circular orbit. Add a small moon to a couple of planets, highlight one planet with a label, and finish with a calm summary line. Use a deep purple space background and bright, rich colours.

name: Fourier Circles Explainer
summary: Rotating circles chained end to end trace a wave that unrolls to the right, in calm 3Blue1Brown style.
bestFor: Signal processing and music-math explainers
prompt: Show how a square wave can be built from rotating circles. Start with one large circle, chain smaller faster circles onto its tip, and let the final tip trace a wave that unrolls to the right. Narrate how adding more circles makes the corners sharper and the wave closer to the target shape.

name: Git Branching Explainer
summary: A branch splits off the main line, collects its own commits, then merges back with a merge commit.
bestFor: Teaching branches and merges to new developers
prompt: Explain how git branching works. Start with a main line of commits, then branch off to work on a feature without touching main. Show the branch collecting its own commits while main moves on. Finish by merging the branch back with a merge commit that joins both histories.

name: Gradient Descent Explainer
summary: A calm 3Blue1Brown-style walk-through: a ball rolls down a loss curve in shrinking steps on a navy grid.
bestFor: Teaching how machine learning models learn
prompt: Explain gradient descent in the style of a math channel. Start with a bowl-shaped loss curve drawn on thin axes. Drop a ball on the slope, show the tangent that points uphill, and step the opposite way. Let each step get smaller as the slope flattens until the ball settles at the minimum. Finish by writing the update rule, w becomes w minus eta times the gradient, and say what the learning rate controls.

name: HTTPS Handshake Explainer
summary: Browser and server swap hello, certificate and key messages, then a lock closes on encrypted traffic.
bestFor: Explaining how a secure connection is set up
prompt: Explain how an HTTPS connection is established. Show the browser and the server exchanging a hello, the server presenting its certificate, and the two sides agreeing on a shared key. Then close a lock and show that everything sent afterwards is encrypted, so anyone watching the wire sees only scrambled data.

name: Isometric Diorama Showcase
summary: A warm miniature workshop floats on a slab while the camera slowly orbits it.
bestFor: Studio tours, maker brands, cozy product stories
prompt: Create a warm showcase of a small creative workshop for a maker brand. Show a tiny isometric room on a floating slab with a desk, a glowing lamp, shelves and a plant while the camera slowly turns around it. Introduce the studio, highlight a few details, and end on a friendly invitation to visit.

name: Exploded View Product Reveal
summary: A mechanical keyboard lifts apart into caps, switches, plate and case, then reassembles while the camera orbits.
bestFor: Hardware reveals that show what is inside
prompt: Create a product reveal for Tactile 60, a fictional compact mechanical keyboard. Open on the assembled board, then lift it apart into keycaps, switches, plate and case while the camera orbits slowly. Explain that every layer is tuned for a quiet, satisfying typing feel, then close the board and show the product name.

name: Kinetic Quote Stack
summary: A short sentence stacks as huge serif lines, word by word, with a highlighted key word and a drawn rule.
bestFor: Pull quotes, mission lines and principles for social and intros
prompt: Turn one short principle into a kinetic quote video: make it simple enough to remember. Set the sentence as a stack of very large lines on a cream background with deep ink type and a single orange accent. Words reveal one by one, the last word gets a highlight, and a thin rule draws beneath it.

name: Kinetic Type Explainer
summary: Single words slam, slide and mask across a bold full-screen poster before stacking into one lockup.
bestFor: Punchy brand statements and idea explainers set purely in type
prompt: Make a fast kinetic typography explainer about our three-step creative process. Each step is one huge word that takes the whole screen in its own colour and typeface: think, design, ship. End on all three words stacked together as a closing lockup with a short beat of music underneath.

name: Linear Transformation Visual
summary: A coordinate grid with basis vectors is sheared and rotated by a matrix as the grid lines bend smoothly.
bestFor: Linear algebra courses, matrix intuition videos
prompt: Explain a two by two matrix as a transformation of space. Show a coordinate grid with the two basis vectors, then apply the matrix so every grid line moves while staying straight and evenly spaced. Point out where each basis vector lands and how the matrix columns record those landing spots.

name: How a Neural Network Learns
summary: Signals pass through three layers while a falling error value reshapes the connection weights.
bestFor: Explaining training, weights and error to a general audience
prompt: Explain how a neural network learns. Show an input layer, a hidden layer and an output layer, and let a signal pass forward through them. Then show the error between the output and the right answer, and how adjusting the connection weights lowers that error with each round of training.

name: Particle Logo Reveal
summary: Thousands of glowing particles swirl in, then lock into a clean ring-and-play mark.
bestFor: Brand intros, app launches, channel openers
prompt: Make a calm brand intro for Lumio, a new video app. Glowing particles drift through a dark space, swirl together and settle into the Lumio mark. Then show the tagline Meet Lumio, hold the logo, and end on a short line inviting people to try it.

name: Procedural Planet Reveal
summary: A rotating planet with noise continents, ocean glints, a glowing atmosphere and a drifting day-night line.
bestFor: Space, game and generative-art showcases
prompt: A slow reveal of a procedurally generated planet turning in space. Continents, oceans and ice caps are shaped by noise, a thin blue atmosphere glows at the edge, city lights flicker on the night side and the sunrise line drifts across the surface against a field of stars. Close on a short line about worlds made from maths.

name: Glossy Product Spin Ad
summary: A glossy 3D drink can spins on a pedestal against a bold gradient with a slow camera push-in.
bestFor: Beverage and packaged-goods launch ads
prompt: Make a calm product ad for Zestly, a fictional sparkling citrus drink. Show the can turning slowly on a pedestal under soft studio light, with a slow push-in. Highlight the bright citrus flavour, the crisp bubbles and the colourful can, then end on the brand name and a short line inviting people to try it.

name: Pub/Sub Queue Explainer
summary: Publishers drop messages in a queue and each message fans out to three subscribers that light up in turn.
bestFor: Explaining message queues and publish-subscribe systems
prompt: Explain how publish and subscribe messaging works. Publishers send messages into a queue without knowing who will read them. The queue holds each message, then fans it out so every subscriber receives its own copy. Explain why this keeps the sending and receiving sides independent of each other.

name: Pythagorean Proof Animation
summary: Four triangles inside a square slide into new places to reveal a squared plus b squared equals c squared.
bestFor: Geometry lessons, proof-without-words shorts
prompt: Prove the Pythagorean theorem with a rearrangement. Draw a square with four copies of one right triangle around a tilted inner square, then slide the triangles into the corners to leave two smaller squares. Show that the same area is left over, and end on the equation a squared plus b squared equals c squared.

name: Terminal Command Screencast
summary: A dark terminal types a build command, prints output, highlights the key line and pops a green check.
bestFor: CLI tutorials, dev-tool demos and how-to walkthroughs
prompt: Make a short screencast showing a developer running one build command in a dark terminal. The command types out character by character, a few lines of output follow, the success line is highlighted, and a green check appears. A calm voiceover explains what the command does and why it matters.

name: Sieve of Eratosthenes Explainer
summary: A quiet number-theory explainer: multiples fade out in colored waves and only the primes stay lit.
bestFor: Number theory intros and math channel explainers
prompt: Explain the sieve of Eratosthenes on a grid of the numbers one to forty-eight. Start with two, keep it, and fade out every multiple of two in one wave. Move to three, then five, each time crossing out its multiples and leaving the number itself. Explain why you can stop once the square of the next number is larger than the grid. Finish with the primes glowing while everything else has faded away.

name: Snow Globe Holiday Greeting
summary: A glass snow globe holds a tiny lit city while seeded snow falls and the whole scene slowly turns.
bestFor: Seasonal greetings and cosy brand moments
prompt: Make a warm holiday greeting for Northlight, a fictional small business. Show a glass snow globe with a tiny lit city inside, snow drifting down and the globe slowly turning on its base. Add a short seasonal message of thanks to customers and finish with the business name and a quiet wish for a peaceful winter.

name: Stick Figure Lesson
summary: A stick figure walks in, points at a hand-drawn bar chart as it draws on, and says a three-word line.
bestFor: Friendly explainers for training and school topics
prompt: Teach why regular practice matters using a simple stick figure. The figure walks in, then points at a hand-drawn chart while four bars are drawn one after another, each taller than the last. A trend arrow is drawn across the bars. The figure ends with a short speech bubble that sums up the lesson. Keep the narration warm, plain and encouraging.

name: Storybook science explainer
summary: A whimsical storybook explainer that follows one character with personality through a long journey.
bestFor: Educators and science channels explaining a process as a tale
prompt: Make a 60-second storybook explainer about a raindrop's journey from cloud to sea. Give the raindrop a charming personality, little visual gags, and onomatopoeia. Show a few honest facts along the way, with a side timeline of what else was happening in the world. Narrated voiceover, burned-in captions, and a gentle score that shifts with each chapter.

name: Milestone Timeline Infographic
summary: A progress line draws across four milestone nodes that light up in turn as the camera pans.
bestFor: Company history, roadmaps and project milestones
prompt: Build a horizontal timeline infographic with four milestones for a made-up project: an idea, a first build, a public launch and a period of growth. Draw a progress line from left to right, light up each milestone with an icon circle and a two-word label as the line reaches it, and pan the camera gently along the track. Finish with every milestone lit and a closing line about the journey.

name: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
summary: A bucket refills one token at a time; each request spends one, and a request is rejected when it runs dry.
bestFor: Explaining rate limiting and traffic shaping to developers
prompt: Explain how a token bucket rate limiter works. Show a bucket that refills with tokens at a steady rate, requests that each spend one token to get through, and what happens when a burst empties the bucket and the next request is rejected. End on why this smooths traffic while still allowing short bursts.

name: Whiteboard Concept Explainer
summary: A hand draws a magnifier over a question mark, an arrow to a lightbulb, then underlines Why?
bestFor: Explaining one idea from scratch to a non-expert audience
prompt: Explain one concept from scratch to someone who has never heard of it. On a whiteboard a hand draws a magnifying glass over a question mark, then an arrow to a lightbulb to show the moment it clicks, then writes the word Why and underlines it. Narrate in a warm, curious voice and keep the language simple.

name: Whiteboard Idea to Launch
summary: A hand sketches doodle icons of a lightbulb, a laptop and a rocket joined by arrows, each labelled.
bestFor: Showing a journey from idea to product launch in three steps
prompt: Show how a product goes from idea to launch on a whiteboard. A hand draws a lightbulb and labels it Idea, then an arrow to a simple laptop labelled Build, then an arrow to a rocket labelled Launch. Add a short voiceover for each step, explaining what happens at that stage in plain, friendly language.

name: Whiteboard Learning Loop
summary: A visible hand writes a title, draws three linked boxes, circles the last in red and loops back.
bestFor: Explaining a process or cycle the way a teacher would
prompt: Explain a simple learning loop on a whiteboard. A hand writes the title, then draws three boxes labelled Plan, Do and Learn joined by arrows. Circle Learn in red, then draw a blue arrow curving back underneath to the start to show the cycle repeats. Narrate each step as it is drawn, in a calm teacher's voice.

name: Zoom Into the Chip
summary: A camera dives from a microchip through layered glowing metal traces toward a blazing core.
bestFor: Hardware, silicon and AI compute announcements
prompt: A dramatic zoom into a microchip. The camera starts above a circuit board, drops through the chip package and down through stacked layers of glowing metal traces, with data pulses racing along them, until it reaches a bright core at the centre. Close on a short line about where the power starts.
